title: Inflation Eases, Defense Pact Takes Shape, and a Quiet Week for Earthquakes
overview: The big domestic news is economic: Turkish inflation fell below 30% for the first time since 2021, lifting bank stocks and sharpening talk of further rate cuts. Regionally, Ankara joined a new Turkey-Pakistan-Saudi defense pact as tensions with Houthi forces continue in the Red Sea, while a cluster of earthquakes near Feke (Adana) caused no damage. A detention case involving a Kurdish Iranian journalist is drawing attention from rights-focused outlets.

sections.heading: Inflation Dips Below 30%
sections.body: September data show Turkish annual inflation falling more than expected, dropping under 30% for the first time since 2021. Markets responded with renewed interest in Turkish bank stocks, and analysts are now discussing the likelihood of further central bank rate cuts. For residents, this is the clearest sign yet that the sharp cost-of-living pressures of recent years may be easing, though exchange rates (USD/TRY 49.16, EUR/TRY 55.11) remain a reminder that recovery is gradual, not sudden.

sections.heading: New Defense Pact With Pakistan and Saudi Arabia
sections.body: Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia held an emergency meeting in Mecca and issued a joint statement on a new mutual defense arrangement, with opposition-leaning outlets reporting pledges of troop deployment to Saudi Arabia amid ongoing Houthi attacks in the Red Sea. State media framed this as a joint defense committee statement; independent and opposition coverage emphasized the troop pledge and the wider Yemen conflict, where Saudi-backed Yemeni forces report securing a key Red Sea waterway. This sits alongside separate safety developments abroad — including reports of Iranian-linked attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and a drone threat that prompted the US to evacuate bombers from a UK base. None of this affects daily life in Türkiye directly, but it's worth watching for residents with regional travel plans.

sections.heading: Earthquakes Near Feke, No Damage
sections.body: Five earthquakes of magnitude 4.2 to 5.0 struck near Feke, in Adana province, on October 4. No damage was reported. This is a normal seismic cluster for the region; residents don't need to change routines, but it's a good reminder to keep emergency supplies current.

sections.heading: Detention Allegations and Residency Procedures
sections.body: A Kurdish Iranian journalist has told Stockholm Center for Freedom and the Jerusalem Post that Turkish guards beat him and pressured him to sign deportation papers; this account currently appears mainly in opposition-leaning and independent outlets and has not been corroborated elsewhere in today's material. Separately, on routine paperwork: international students at Trakya University and Anadolu University had fingerprints collected for residence permits (ikamet) through in-person visits from Migration Authority staff rather than requiring a trip to the local office — a small but welcome convenience noted in Turkish-language press.

closing: Stay dry, keep your paperwork handy, and here's to calmer inflation numbers — see you tomorrow.
